sentences.text: The Second respondent in M.C.O.P.No.721 of 2014 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Additional District and Special Court, Pudukkottai, filed this appeal, challenging the award passed in the said M.C.O.P.No.721 of 2014 filed by the respondents 1 to 4 herein.

sentences.text: 2.Facts of the case:
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Fifth Respondent namely, Jeya is the owner of the car bearing Registration No.TN-49 AT-0786.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: On 31.05.2014 at 11.15 p.m., the said vehicle was taken by her father Mahendran, along with his brother-in-law deceased/Neelakandan towards Trichy to Peravoorani Road.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: At that time, near Vadakadu AV Petrol bunk, the Mini Lorry, namely the insured lorry bearing Registration No.TN-55 AE-2460, was driven by the driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car, thereby the deceased sustained injuries.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: After treatment for 26 days, he died.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Vadakadu Police Station registered a case in Crime No. 69 of 2014 against the lorry driver insured with the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, the wife of the deceased and his legal heirs filed MCOP No.721 of 2014 stating that the accident happened due to the negligence of both the drivers.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The deceased Neelakandan was doing Coconut business earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month and claimed compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-
(Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs Only).
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Income certificate/Ex.P.16 was marked and the Vice President of Cultivation and Marketing of Coconuts Association namely, P.W.3 was examined.

entities.text: Cultivation and Marketing of Coconuts Association
entities.label: ORG

sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: P.W.3 stated that he is the vice president of Peravoorani Coconut Farmer Association.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis deceased/Neelakandan was in the said business for 10 years and earned more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: appellant insurance company filed a counter denying the negligence on the part of insured lorry and shifting the negligence on the part of the car driver.

sentences.text: Hence,appellant seeks for exoneration from the liability and also disputed the income of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. During the course of the trial, the claimant proved their claim, and examined P.W.1 to 4 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the side of the respondent/appellant insurance company, R.W.1 was examined and Ex.R1 was marked.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
5.The learned trial Judge considered the entire evidence, more particularly, the evidence of R.W.1,
who drove the mini-lorry on the date of the occurrence, who pleaded guilty and fixed the liability upon the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis appellant insured vehicle namely the mini-lorry.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, the insurance company filed this appeal challenging the fixing of negligence on the part of the lorry driver in spite of the pleadings that both drivers of the vehicles were responsible for the accident.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6.The learned counsel for the appellant reiterated grounds filed in the affidavit stating that the plea of guilty before the criminal Court and conviction is not a circumstance to fix the entire liability on the appellant against the pleadings.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel further submitted that without any sufficient income proof, the learned trial Judge erroneously fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 20,000/- per month and hence, he seeks for the reduction of the compensation awarded by the Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The learned trial Judge erred in relying on the result of the criminal case in these proceedings and hence he seeks for the interference in the award.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7.Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 submitted that when there is a plea of guilty and conviction was passed in the criminal case, the Judgement can https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis be marked to show that there was admission relating to the negligence.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, the said admission has to be properly explained by the driver of the said vehicle.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In this case, even though R.W.1 was examined, no explanation was given by R.W.1 under what circumstances, he pleaded guilty and paid the fine.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, he seeks for the affirmation of the finding relating to the negligence on the part of the driver.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel further submitted that P.W.3 was examined and also Ex.P.16 was marked and the specific pleading was that the deceased was doing coconut business.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence, the learned trial Judge fixed Rs.20,000/- as monthly income and there is no reason to differ with the same without any contra evidence adduced on the side of the Insurance company.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks for non interference in the award passed by the Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Even otherwise, he said that the learned trial Judge without considering the future prospect granted only Rs.20,000/- as monthly income.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: If future prospects are added, there can not be reduction of the amount.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, he seeks for the confirmation of the award.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8.We have considered rival submissions and also perused the evidence and the impugned Judgement and also precedents relied upon both parties.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
9.Whether the tribunal is correct in fixing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, who had pleaded guilty before the criminal Court?
9.1.Whether the award granted by the tribunal is just and reasonable?
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 10. R.W.1 is the driver of the appellant insurance company's insured vehicle.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The criminal case was registered against him and a final report was filed against him and he paid the fine after plea of guilty.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Even though R.W.1 was examined and he pleaded guilty, he did not properly explain the admission of rash and negligent driving.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: This Court finds no explanation on the side of R.W.1 for the above admission.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Honourable Supreme Court, this Court and various High Courts and even the English Courts have held that if a party pleaded guilty before the Court, the same is admissible as a admission to the fact of the case, unless https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the same was explained otherwise by him.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
11.In the said circumstances, the following judgments of the Honorable Supreme Court and our High Court are to be considered:-
11.1.1

sentences.text: The above judgments have held that when the accused pleaded guilty, the criminal Court judgment is admissible.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The fact of negligence was admitted by plea of guilty.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, the same has to be properly explained by the concerned person.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Otherwise, the said admission relating to the factum of negligence can very well relied by the Tribunal to render the findings on negligence as against the driver of the vehicle.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: 11.2. When the accused pleaded guilty by admitting his rashness and negligence and caused accident before the Criminal Court during the prosecution of the corresponding criminal offence.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The same is admissible as fact to prove the issue of negligence in the civil proceedings unless he has properly explained the said admission to the satisfaction Court.
sentences._hearing_file: The Branch Manager vs Kala on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
In the case of Nettleship Vs. Weston,
reported in 11.3. 1972 ACJ 115, Lord Denning has held as follows:
5...The conviction is admissible in civil proceedings as prima facie evidence of negligence...

opennyai_summary.facts:
The deceased Neelakandan was doing Coconut business earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month and claimed compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-
(Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs Only).
appellant insurance company filed a counter denying the negligence on the part of insured lorry and shifting the negligence on the part of the car driver.
Hence,appellant seeks for exoneration from the liability and also disputed the income of the deceased.
The insurance company, who insured the car also filed a counter stating that the accident happened only due to the negligence of mini-lorry driver, and pleaded for exoneration from liability against the car driver.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In this case, even though R.W.1 was examined, no explanation was given by R.W.1 under what circumstances, he pleaded guilty and paid the fine.
In the said circumstances, he seeks for the affirmation of the finding relating to the negligence on the part of the driver.
Hence, the learned trial Judge fixed Rs.20,000/- as monthly income and there is no reason to differ with the same without any contra evidence adduced on the side of the Insurance company.
opennyai_summary.issue:
9.Whether the tribunal is correct in fixing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, who had pleaded guilty before the criminal Court?
9.1.Whether the award granted by the tribunal is just and reasonable?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even though R.W.1 was examined and he pleaded guilty, he did not properly explain the admission of rash and negligent driving.
The fact of negligence was admitted by plea of guilty.
In the said circumstances, the same has to be properly explained by the concerned person.
Otherwise, the said admission relating to the factum of negligence can very well relied by the Tribunal to render the findings on negligence as against the driver of the vehicle.
11.2. When the accused pleaded guilty by admitting his rashness and negligence and caused accident before the Criminal Court during the prosecution of the corresponding criminal offence.
The same is admissible as fact to prove the issue of negligence in the civil proceedings unless he has properly explained the said admission to the satisfaction Court.
11.5. In the case of Seth Ramdayal Jat v. Laxmi Prasad, reported in (2009) 11 SCC 545 at page 553, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as follows:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 21.
An admission against bis interest made by R.W. 1 either before the Tribunal or elsewhere, has got to be taken into account in rendering a decision on the relative stands taken by the parties in the controversy.
This Court has ruled in the case, Vinobabai v. K.S.R.T.C., (1979) 1 Kant LJ 257 that when the driver admits his guilt before the Criminal Court and is convicted, it would establish prima facie that he was guilty of rash and negligent driving and we have pointed out above that the driver did not care to enter the witness-box and offer any explanation
The admission, therefore, becomes https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis decisive on the facts of the present case that the accident was the result of rash and negligent driving of the car in question by its driver.
In the said circumstances, fixing of Rs.20,000/- as a monthly income by the tribunal is to be confirmed.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Further, the learned trial Judge ordered only Rs.20,000/- without considering the future prospect.
If future prospect is considered, the amount would go around Rs.8,00,000/-.
In the said circumstances, this court finds no merit in the appeal.
This appeal is dismissed and the judgment and award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Additional District and Special Court, Pudukkottai in M.C.O.P.No.721 of 2014, dated 29.06.2018 is hereby confirmed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected civil miscellaneous petition is closed.
